iti śrībṛhannanāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsapratipadvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma daśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.110.d:
व्रतेष्वेतेषु सर्वेषु ब्रह्मचर्यं विधीयते ।
भोजने तु हविष्यान्नं सामान्यत उदाहृतम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्ननारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासप्रतिपद्व्रतनिरूपणं नाम दशोत्तरशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.110.m:
In all these vows, celibacy is prescribed; / for food, sacrificial food is generally prescribed.

Thus ends the one hundred and tenth chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Vows on the First Days of the Twelve Months,' in the fourth quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.111.s:
sanātana uvāca
śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi dvitīyāyā vratāni te /
yāni kṛtvā naro bhaktyā brahmaloke mahīyate //
1.111.d:
सनातन उवाच
शृणु विप्र प्रवक्ष्यामि द्वितीयाया व्रतानि ते ।
यानि कृत्वा नरो भक्त्या ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
1.111.m: Sanātana said: / Listen, O Brahmin, I will declare to you the vows of the second lunar day, / performing which with devotion a man is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

1.111.s:
caitraśukladvitīyāyāṃ brahmaṇaṃ ca saśaktikam /
haviṣyānnena gandhādyaiḥ stoṣya sarvakratūdbhavam //
1.111.d:
चैत्रशुक्लद्वितीयायां ब्रह्मणं च सशक्तिकम् ।
हविष्यान्नेन गन्धाद्यैः स्तोष्य सर्वक्रतूद्भवम् ॥
1.111.m: On the second day of the bright half of Caitra, praising Brahmā together with his Śakti / with sacrificial food, perfumes, and the like, [one attains] the fruit arising from all sacrifices;

1.111.s:
phalaṃ labdhvākhilānkāmānante brahmapadaṃ labhet /
asminneva dine vipra bālendumuditaṃ pare //
1.111.d:
फलं लब्ध्वाखिलान्कामानन्ते ब्रह्मपदं लभेत् ।
अस्मिन्नेव दिने विप्र बालेन्दुमुदितं परे ॥
1.111.m: having attained all desires, at the end he reaches the station of Brahmā. / On this very day, O Brahmin, having worshipped the newly risen crescent moon

1.111.s:
samabhyarcya niśāraṃbhe bhuktimuktiphalaṃ bhavet /
atha vāsmindine bhaktyā dasrāvabhyarcya yatnataḥ //
1.111.d:
समभ्यर्च्य निशारंभे भुक्तिमुक्तिफलं भवेत् ।
अथ वास्मिन्दिने भक्त्या दस्रावभ्यर्च्य यत्नतः ॥
1.111.m: at the beginning of the night on the following [day], the fruit is enjoyment and liberation. / Alternatively, on this day, having worshipped the two Dasras with devotion and care,

1.111.s:
suvarṇarajate netre pradadyācca dvijātaye /
pūrṇayātrāvrate hyasmindadhnā vāpi ghṛtena ca //
1.111.d:
सुवर्णरजते नेत्रे प्रदद्याच्च द्विजातये ।
पूर्णयात्राव्रते ह्यस्मिन्दध्ना वापि घृतेन च ॥
1.111.m: one should give eyes of gold and silver to a twice-born. / In this vow of complete journey, indeed with curd or with ghee,

1.111.s:
netravrataṃ dvādaśa vatsarānvai kṛtyā bhavedbhūmipatirdvijendra /
surūparūpo 'rigaṇapratāpī dharmābhirāmo nṛpavargamukhyaḥ //
1.111.d:
नेत्रव्रतं द्वादश वत्सरान्वै कृत्या भवेद्भूमिपतिर्द्विजेन्द्र ।
सुरूपरूपो ऽरिगणप्रतापी धर्माभिरामो नृपवर्गमुख्यः ॥
1.111.m: By performing the netravrata for twelve years, O best of twice-born, / one becomes an earthly ruler, endowed with handsome form, burning up hordes of foes, delighting in righteousness, foremost among kings.

1.111.s:
rādhaśukladvitīyāyāṃ brahmaṇaṃ viṣṇurūpiṇam /
samarcya saptadhānyānyāḍhyakuṃbhopari vidhānataḥ //
1.111.d:
राधशुक्लद्वितीयायां ब्रह्मणं विष्णुरूपिणम् ।
समर्च्य सप्तधान्यान्याढ्यकुंभोपरि विधानतः ॥
1.111.m: On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, having duly worshipped Brahmā in the form of Viṣṇu / upon a water-jar filled with the seven grains,

1.111.s:
viṣṇulokamavāpnoti bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān /
jyeṣṭhaśukladvitīyāyāṃ bhāskaraṃ bhuvanādhipam //
1.111.d:
विष्णुलोकमवाप्नोति भुक्त्वा भोगान्मनोरमान् ।
ज्येष्ठशुक्लद्वितीयायां भास्करं भुवनाधिपम् ॥
1.111.m: one attains the world of Viṣṇu after enjoying delightful pleasures. / On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, having duly worshipped the sun, the lord of the world,

1.111.s:
catuvaktrasvarūpaṃ ca samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ /
bhojayitvā dvijān bhaktyā bhāskaraṃ lokamāpnuyāt //
1.111.d:
चतुवक्त्रस्वरूपं च समभ्यर्च्य विधानतः ।
भोजयित्वा द्विजान् भक्त्या भास्करं लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.111.m: in the form of the four-faced one [Brahmā], / and having fed the twice-born with devotion, one attains the world of the sun.

1.111.s:
āṣāḍhasya site pakṣe dvitīyā puṇyasaṃyutā /
tasyāṃ rathaṃ samāropya rāmaṃ saha subhadrayā //
1.111.d:
आषाढस्य सिते पक्षे द्वितीया पुण्यसंयुता ।
तस्यां रथं समारोप्य रामं सह सुभद्रया ॥
1.111.m: In the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha is the meritorious second lunar day. / On that day, having mounted Rāma along with Subhadrā onto a chariot,

1.111.s:
dvijādibhirvratī sārdhaṃ parikramya purādikam /
jalāśayāntikaṃ gatvā kārayecca mahotsavam //
1.111.d:
द्विजादिभिर्व्रती सार्धं परिक्रम्य पुरादिकम् ।
जलाशयान्तिकं गत्वा कारयेच्च महोत्सवम् ॥
1.111.m: the observer of the vow, accompanied by the twice-born and others, having circumambulated the city and other places / and having gone to the vicinity of a reservoir of water, should perform a great festival.

1.111.s:
tadante devabhavane niveśya ca yathāvidhi /
brāhmaṇānbhojayeccaiva vratasyāsya prapūrtaye //
1.111.d:
तदन्ते देवभवने निवेश्य च यथाविधि ।
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेच्चैव व्रतस्यास्य प्रपूर्तये ॥
1.111.m: Then, having placed [the deities] in a temple according to rule, / he should feed the brāhmaṇas for the complete fulfillment of this vow.

1.111.s:
nabhaḥ śukladvitīyāyāṃ viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ /
svapitīti tithiḥ puṇyā hyaśokaśayanāhvayā //
1.111.d:
नभः शुक्लद्वितीयायां विश्वकर्मा प्रजापतिः ।
स्वपितीति तिथिः पुण्या ह्यशोकशयनाह्वया ॥
1.111.m: On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Śrāvaṇa, Viśvakarman Prajāpati / goes to sleep; hence this meritorious lunar day is called Aśokaśayanā.

1.111.s:
saśaktika tu śayyāsthaṃ pūjayitvā caturmukham /
imamuccārayenmantraṃ praṇamya jagatāṃ patim //
1.111.d:
सशक्तिक तु शय्यास्थं पूजयित्वा चतुर्मुखम् ।
इममुच्चारयेन्मन्त्रं प्रणम्य जगतां पतिम् ॥
1.111.m: Having worshipped the four-faced one lying on a couch together with his consort, / and having bowed down to the lord of the worlds, one should utter this mantra:

1.111.s:
śrīvatsadhāriñchrīkānta śrīvāsa śrīpate prabho /
gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmada //
1.111.d:
श्रीवत्सधारिञ्छ्रीकान्त श्रीवास श्रीपते प्रभो ।
गार्हस्थ्यं मा प्रणाशं मे यातु धर्मार्थकामद ॥
1.111.m: “O bearer of the Śrīvatsa, beloved of Śrī, abode of Śrī, lord of Śrī, O master, / bestower of righteousness, wealth, and desire, may my householder life not go to ruin!”

1.111.s:
candrārddhadānamatroktaṃ sarvasiddhividhāyakam /
bhādraśukladvitīyāyāṃ śakrarūpaṃ jagadvidhim //
1.111.d:
चन्द्रार्द्धदानमत्रोक्तं सर्वसिद्धिविधायकम् ।
भाद्रशुक्लद्वितीयायां शक्ररूपं जगद्विधिम् ॥
1.111.m: Here, giving a crescent moon is declared to bring about all success. / On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada, having worshipped the creator of the world in the form of Indra

1.111.s:
pūjayitvā vidhānenana sarvakratuphalaṃ labhet /
āśvine māsi vai puṇyā dvitīyā śuklapakṣagā //
1.111.d:
पूजयित्वा विधानेनन सर्वक्रतुफलं लभेत् ।
आश्विने मासि वै पुण्या द्वितीया शुक्लपक्षगा ॥
1.111.m: according to rule, one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices. / In the month of Āśvina, the second lunar day occurring in the bright fortnight is meritorious;

1.111.s:
dānaṃ pradattametasyāmanantaphalamucyate /
ūrjjaśukladvitīyāyāṃ yamo yamunayā purā //
1.111.d:
दानं प्रदत्तमेतस्यामनन्तफलमुच्यते ।
ऊर्ज्जशुक्लद्वितीयायां यमो यमुनया पुरा ॥
1.111.m: a gift given on this day is said to yield endless fruit. / On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, Yama was formerly

1.111.s:
bhojitaḥ svagṛhe tena dvitīyaiṣā yamāhvayā /
puṣṭipravarddhanaṃ cātra bhaginyā bhojanaṃ gṛhe //
1.111.d:
भोजितः स्वगृहे तेन द्वितीयैषा यमाह्वया ।
पुष्टिप्रवर्द्धनं चात्र भगिन्या भोजनं गृहे ॥
1.111.m: fed by Yamunā in her own house; therefore, this second lunar day is named after Yama. / Eating in the house of a sister here promotes nourishment.

1.111.s: vastrālaṅkārapūrvaṃ tu tasmai deyamataḥ param //
1.111.d: वस्त्रालङ्कारपूर्वं तु तस्मै देयमतः परम् ॥
1.111.m: Then, preceded by garments and ornaments, [gifts] should be given to him after that.

1.111.s:
yasyāṃ tithau yamunayā yamarājadevaḥ saṃbhojito nijakarātsvasṛsauhṛdena /
tasyāṃ svasuḥ karatalādiha yo bhunakti prāpnoti ratnadhanadhānyamanuttamaṃ saḥ //
1.111.d:
यस्यां तिथौ यमुनया यमराजदेवः संभोजितो निजकरात्स्वसृसौहृदेन ।
तस्यां स्वसुः करतलादिह यो भुनक्ति प्राप्नोति रत्नधनधान्यमनुत्तमं सः ॥
1.111.m: On the lunar day when Lord Yamarāja was fed by Yamunā from her own hand out of sisterly affection, / he who eats from the hand of a sister on that day obtains incomparable jewels, wealth, and grain.

1.111.s:
mārgaśukladvitīyāyāṃ śrāddhena pitṛpūjanam /
ārogyaṃ labhate cāpi putrapautrasamanvayaḥ //
1.111.d:
मार्गशुक्लद्वितीयायां श्राद्धेन पितृपूजनम् ।
आरोग्यं लभते चापि पुत्रपौत्रसमन्वयः ॥
1.111.m: On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, worship of the ancestors through a śrāddha / brings health, and one is endowed with sons and grandsons.

1.111.s:
pauṣaśukladvitīyāyāṃ gośṛṅgodakamārjanam /
sarvakāmapradaṃ nṝṇāmāste bālendudarśanam //
1.111.d:
पौषशुक्लद्वितीयायां गोशृङ्गोदकमार्जनम् ।
सर्वकामप्रदं नॄणामास्ते बालेन्दुदर्शनम् ॥
1.111.m: On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa, sprinkling with water from a cow’s horn / grants all desires to mortals; viewing the crescent moon is also [performed].

1.111.s:
yor'ghyadānena bālenduṃ haviṣyāśī jitendriyaḥ /
pūjayetsājyasumanedharmakāmārthasiddhaye //
1.111.d:
योर्ऽघ्यदानेन बालेन्दुं हविष्याशी जितेन्द्रियः ।
पूजयेत्साज्यसुमनेधर्मकामार्थसिद्धये ॥
1.111.m: He who, subsisting on sacrificial food with senses conquered, / worships the crescent moon by offering arghya along with clarified butter and flowers, achieves righteousness, desire, and wealth.

1.111.s:
māghaśukladvitīyāyāṃ bhānurūpaṃ prajāpatim /
samabhyarcya yathānyāyaṃ pūjayedraktapuṣpakaiḥ //
1.111.d:
माघशुक्लद्वितीयायां भानुरूपं प्रजापतिम् ।
समभ्यर्च्य यथान्यायं पूजयेद्रक्तपुष्पकैः ॥
1.111.m: On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, having duly honoured Prajāpati in the form of the sun, / one should worship him with red flowers

1.111.s:
raktairgaṃvaistathā svarṇamūrtiṃ nirmāya śaktitaḥ /
tataḥ pūrṇaṃ tāmrapātraṃ gāghṛmairvāpitaṇḍulaiḥ //
1.111.d:
रक्तैर्गंवैस्तथा स्वर्णमूर्तिं निर्माय शक्तितः ।
ततः पूर्णं ताम्रपात्रं गाघृमैर्वापितण्डुलैः ॥
1.111.m: and red perfumes, having fashioned a golden image according to one's means. / Then, having offered a copper vessel filled with saffron or rice grains

1.111.s:
samarpya deve bhaktyaiva sa mūrtiṃ pradadeddvije /
evaṃ kṛte vrate vipra sākṣātsūrya ivoditaḥ //
1.111.d:
समर्प्य देवे भक्त्यैव स मूर्तिं प्रददेद्द्विजे ।
एवं कृते व्रते विप्र साक्षात्सूर्य इवोदितः ॥
1.111.m: to the deity with devotion, he should give that image to a twice-born. / When the vow is thus performed, O twice-born, like the sun visibly risen,

1.111.s:
durāsado durādharṣo jāyate bhuvimānavaḥ /
iha kāmānvarāmbhuktvā yātyante brahmaṇaḥ padam //
1.111.d:
दुरासदो दुराधर्षो जायते भुविमानवः ।
इह कामान्वराम्भुक्त्वा यात्यन्ते ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥
1.111.m: a mortal becomes difficult of approach and invincible in the world. / Having enjoyed excellent desires here, he goes at the end to the abode of Brahmā.

1.111.s:
sarvadevastuto 'bhīkṣṇaṃ vimānavaramāsthitaḥ /
atha phaālgunaśuklāyā dvitīyāyāṃ dvijottamaḥ //
1.111.d:
सर्वदेवस्तुतो ऽभीक्ष्णं विमानवरमास्थितः ।
अथ फआल्गुनशुक्लाया द्वितीयायां द्विजोत्तमः ॥
1.111.m: Constantly praised by all the gods, seated in an excellent aerial chariot. / Then, on the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, the best of the twice-born,

1.111.s:
puṣpaiḥ śivaṃ samabhyarcya suśvetaiśca sugandhibhaḥ /
puṣpairvitānakaṃ kṛtvā puṣpālaṅkaraṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.111.d:
पुष्पैः शिवं समभ्यर्च्य सुश्वेतैश्च सुगन्धिभः ।
पुष्पैर्वितानकं कृत्वा पुष्पालङ्करणैः शुभैः ॥
1.111.m: having worshipped Śiva with pure white, fragrant flowers, / having made a canopy of flowers, along with auspicious floral ornaments,

1.111.s:
naivedyairvividhairdhūpairdīparnīrājanādibhiḥ /
prasādya praṇameccaiva sāṣṭāṅgaṃ patito bhuvi //
1.111.d:
नैवेद्यैर्विविधैर्धूपैर्दीपर्नीराजनादिभिः ।
प्रसाद्य प्रणमेच्चैव साष्टाङ्गं पतितो भुवि ॥
1.111.m: with various food-offerings, incenses, lamps, waving of lights, and other rites, / having propitiated him, should bow down prostrate on the ground.

1.111.s:
evamabhyarcya deveśaṃ martyo vyādhivivarjitaḥ /
dhanadhānyasamāyukto jīvedvirṣaśataṃ dhruvam //
1.111.d:
एवमभ्यर्च्य देवेशं मर्त्यो व्याधिविवर्जितः ।
धनधान्यसमायुक्तो जीवेद्विर्षशतं ध्रुवम् ॥
1.111.m: Having thus worshipped the lord of gods, a mortal, free from disease / and endowed with wealth and grain, certainly lives for a hundred years.

1.111.s:
yadvidhānaṃ dvitīyāsu śuklapakṣagatāsu vā /
proktaṃ tadeva kṛṣṇāsu karttavyaṃ vidhikovidaiḥ //
1.111.d:
यद्विधानं द्वितीयासु शुक्लपक्षगतासु वा ।
प्रोक्तं तदेव कृष्णासु कर्त्तव्यं विधिकोविदैः ॥
1.111.m: Whatever procedure was prescribed for the second lunar days of the bright fortnight, / that very same [procedure] should be performed on those of the dark fortnight by those skilled in ritual rules.

1.111.s:
vahnireva pṛthaṅmāḥsu nānārūpavapurddharaḥ /
pūjyate hi dvitīyāsu brahmacaryyādi pūrvavat //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsadvitīyāvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikādaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.111.d:
वह्निरेव पृथङ्माःसु नानारूपवपुर्द्धरः ।
पूज्यते हि द्वितीयासु ब्रह्मचर्य्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासद्वितीयाव्रतनिरूपणं नामैकादशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.111.m:
Indeed, Fire alone, assuming various forms and bodies, is worshipped in the different months / on the second lunar days; celibacy and the rest are as before.

Thus ends the one hundred and eleventh chapter, named 'Description of the Vow of the Second Lunar Day for the Twelve Months', in the fourth quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
